content.thinking:
I'm checking the sandbox setup and working directory before writing the file, then planning out the imports I'll need—geometry helpers, curve utilities, and SVG texture generation—before drafting the bird animation frames.

Now I'm working out the bird's pose geometry: defining a center point, figuring out its forward-facing direction with a slight upward tilt typical of a perched bird, and setting up a local coordinate frame (right, forward, up) so I can place body parts like the torso relative to that joint.

I'm sketching the body as an elongated sphere oriented along the bird's forward axis, then adding a lighter belly patch and planning a countershading paint scheme (blue top, cream underside) so the sphere's surface gets natural gradient coloring based on world normals, before starting on the head sphere placement.

Now I'm working out the head details: cheek patches as flattened spheres, an upper and lower beak built from cones with the lower jaw posed open at an angle, plus small black-and-white eye spheres, crest spikes jutting back from the skull, and the start of a teardrop-shaped wing outline extruded along the body sides.

Defining wing orientation vectors...

Working out the tail geometry so it lies flat with the thickness axis pointing up, then shaping a forked outline with sharp points that stay convex without crossing, plus a gradient paint darkening toward the tip.

I'm adding thin orange leg rods from the belly to a perch point on the capybara's skull, with tiny toe rods for feet, computing the crown position dynamically via a surface ray-cast so the bird sits correctly on top.

I'm placing a flower behind the left ear using an angular offset from the skull center, positioning the eyes symmetrically around the head, and adding sparse whisker rods on the muzzle sides curved outward using surface-normal directions.

For the nose, I'm adding squashed dark spheres for nostrils and a gradient blend near the nose tip to darken that region into brown, then placing small cream incisor boxes peeking from the upper lip.

For the jaw and nose detail, I'm using a skull surface ray to position the nose tip accurately, aligning the chin slightly behind it, and adding a philtrum via a decal — a dark rounded nose pad shape with a lighter center split line projected onto the front face.

Now I'm shifting to designing the mouth: a smile decal running along the muzzle side, curving from the front lip backward and upward toward the cheek, using an SVG path oriented for the left side projection.

I need to work out the mirroring for the right side, since the view direction flips the sense of "left" and "right" relative to the drawing's coordinate axes — so the decal needs to be mirrored when applied to the opposite side of the model.

Working through the other side: with dir [-1,0,0], the right side faces +Z (front), meaning the drawing's left edge corresponds to the back, so mirroring is needed there. I'll verify this in preview, then sketch the smile path, a curve running from front to back with an upward curl, plus a small dimple stroke near the end.

For blush, I'm placing pink ellipses on the lower-rear cheek area using approximate skull angles, sized small, colored solid since alpha blending isn't available, possibly adding a few darker hatching lines for texture. For whisker pores or freckle dots, I'm considering folding a few tiny dots into the muzzle/smile decal rather than making a separate texture layer.

Now I'm thinking through eyebrows — small cream/tan tufts arcing over the eyes — deciding to skip full sweeps and instead scatter a small cluster region. Then I'm working out the ear geometry, sketching a rounded fold outline and figuring out how to orient the extrusion plane so the ear sits correctly as a sideways-facing disk rather than a flat forward plate.

For the ears I'll layer a dark outer slab with a smaller pink slab offset outward along the side axis, giving that rim-with-pink-skin look rodents have. I'll place the flower behind the left ear on the +X side.

Next I'm thinking through body fur cards along the body loft, deciding capybaras don't need a mane, and considering whether to add subtle mottling or saddle markings before moving to small details like webbed membranes between the toes using thin extruded slabs.

Switching to toe geometry, I'm defining each foot's toe joints branching off the leg's tip joint, spreading four toes at slight x offsets with a forward fan, tapering each as a thin capsule from base to tip and adding small dark nail caps.

Still writing paw/toe placement code... and then I'll need to adjust vertical targets so the paw and toe bottoms line up near the floor contact point before moving on to the body code.

Now I'm defining the color palette: coat tones, belly, nose, ear, dark accents, eye and teeth colors, plus the capybara's incisor tint and a separate blue/cream palette for the bird.

Working through joint structure now, figuring out how the head attaches to the neck chain's last joint and how the spine chain should parent off the hips for the skinned loft body.

I'm deciding whether to include the hips joint explicitly in the bone chain or just let spine and neck suffice, treating any leftover rump geometry as owned by the first joint. I'm also thinking about adding chubby thigh spheres near the hip joints to give the legs a stumpy, capybara-like look.

Now I'm working out card counts and density across body, head, and leg regions to keep the mesh clean without triggering warnings, then moving into writing the actual generation code. I'm setting up a helper for raycasting and establishing a sign convention (sx = +1 for the model's left side) that I'll use consistently when positioning eyes and limbs symmetrically.

Working out the eye placement math...

For the lid I'll give it a darker brown than the coat for definition, and position two highlight glints—one larger and one smaller offset—to catch the light on the eyeball's curve. Then I'm moving on to brow ridge cards, cheek tufts, and figuring out where to place the nose decal relative to the tip.

For the nose I'm casting a ray to find the surface hit point and sizing the decal to match the nose width. Then for the jaw I'm setting up a joint and bone sweep path with a tapering radius, countershaded lighter toward the chin to suggest the belly coloring.

I'm considering adding a small chin sphere and whether to slightly open the jaw for a mouth gap, but leaning toward keeping the rest pose closed and neutral. Now I'm planning the whiskers -- computing base hit points on the skull per side, angling each spike's direction back and down from the surface normal, and adding a couple extra whiskers on the jaw, before moving on to fur cards for the tail.

Working out flower geometry now: placing the center slightly off the surface along the normal, then arranging petals in a ring using frame orientation so each petal's thickness axis points outward along the normal, with a simple polygon outline defining the petal shape.

Since bone defaults to nearest joint when empty, passing bone: head explicitly is the safer choice. I'll skip stems and leaves for simplicity, and handle bird feet with toe ray hits. Now I'm ready to write out the full file, being careful about the ear extrude orientation.
